patch.value: The fleet's own mandatory gates as the first sim-to-RL environment

The honest version of recursive self-improvement for this ecosystem is not a claim about general capability, it is a measurable loop the fleet already runs by hand. An agent proposes a change to a pm package; the package's own mandatory gates decide whether it passed. Those gates are unusually well suited to being a reward because they were built to be uncheatable for a different reason: exact coverage thresholds, docstring coverage, acceptance scripts that run the built artifact, and bot review rounds that must be resolved rather than dismissed. The environment is the repository at a pinned commit, the action is a diff, and the reward is the gate verdict, which is already deterministic and already recorded. Registering that as a pm-rl environment turns the fleet's own review history into training and evaluation data with complete provenance, and it makes the sim-to-real gap concrete: gate-pass rate in the sandboxed environment against merge rate on real pull requests.

The environment specification pins the repository commit, the gate command set, and the verdict extraction, and is content-addressed like every other environment; a recorded episode replays to the same verdict on the same commit; the sim-to-real report contrasts sandbox gate-pass rate with real pull-request merge rate over the same period; no episode captures repository credentials or hosted service data
